shortName: University of Arizona College of Medicine - Phoenix
additionalCoursework:
Behavioral Sciences: Two (2) courses in any of the following: cultural anthropology, economics, health care administration, psychology, sociology, public policy, family studies, history, political science, social work, behavioral health, gender studies. 4 credit hours minimum. P/F not accepted, AP credit accepted, Online courses accepted, community college courses accepted.

Humanities: One (1) course in any of the following: art, music, theater, speech and communication, philosophy, religion, ethics, literature, etc. 2 credit hours minimum. P/F not accepted, AP credit accepted, Online courses accepted, community college courses accepted.

Notes: one course (2 credit hours minimum) in Chemistry or Biology must be upper-division. A course is satisfied when completed with a grade of “C” (2.00) or better. Coursework must be completed no later than the Spring Semester/Quarter prior to matriculation. AP credits only accepted if they appear on an official college transcript.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity: The mission of the Office of Health Care Advancement is to provide pathways for the recruitment and retention of trainees who seek to serve the people of Arizona; to provide education that gives the tools to faculty, trainees, and staff to deliver the best care to all patients; and support research that advances knowledge and application for improved community health outcomes and reduction of preventable disease. To facilitate this, connecting with community both inside the University of Arizona and building partnerships with community-based organizations is central to understanding the evolving needs of patients to advance health care for all.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: For a complete listing of all student policies at the College of Medicine - Phoenix, visit http://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/students/student-affairs
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: The UA College of Medicine – Phoenix has an extremely active student body which is engaged in the future of medicine, patient care and education by virtue of activism and professional development in all specialties. There are student interest groups, community groups, as well as student mentoring and wellness programs. Each student group has a specific focus and desire to collaborate with practicing physicians, academicians and peers through speaking engagements, clinics and other exciting hands-on events. The College empowers and encourages students to engage in their community at every level including having students sit on almost every committee (admissions, curriculum, honor code, student progress, etc.). The College also hosts student leadership retreats, therapy dogs, the Wellness Olympics, simulation center events, and off campus social gatherings. There are plenty of opportunities to engage with your fellow classmates. Learn more at https://www.uacomps.org/orgs
medSchoolStudLife.setting:
The college has called Phoenix home since becoming a regional campus in 1992. One of the largest metropolitan areas, Phoenix is comprised of over 20 cities and plays host to over 4.5 million people, a number complimented by the millions more who visit annually. It is also known for its year-round sunshine, desert and mountain landscapes, educational assets, professional sports and dynamic culture.

The U of A College of Medicine – Phoenix is part of the Phoenix Bioscience Core (PBC), a city initiative bringing bioresearch and education to downtown. The State of Arizona and City of Phoenix, as well as other vital community partners, continue to be strong supporters of the college, intent on developing the PBC as a major biosciences hub and premier provider of medical education.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: With the downtown Phoenix landscape continuing to expand, the housing options for students have, as well. Currently there are multiple apartment complexes within walking distance of the campus, and more are nearing completion. The plethora of options gives students the power of choice.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems:
The LGBTQ in Medicine student interest group serves our campus' connection to the LGBTQ community in Phoenix. With a focus on LGBTQ health and social issues, the group seeks to foster a welcoming, supportive environment for our students and offer education about the health issues and difficulties affecting LGBTQ individuals, their families, and communities. The group is dedicated to keeping the student body informed about issues surrounding the LGBTQ community by hosting social events, guest speakers, patient panels, and connecting students with LGBTQ events and service opportunities throughout the Valley.

Our Office of Health Care Advancement also offers MedSafeZone and Transgender Affirming Healthcare training opportunities.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Our Disability Resource Center is the official department designated by the University of Arizona to determine and provide access to classes, programs, and activities for students with disabilities. Students who experience physical or academic barriers based on a temporary or chronic medical condition or disability can contact the DRC for support, including assistance with receiving accommodations for block exams and shelf exams.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms: More information regarding our wellness program can be found here: https://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/wellness
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
The University of Arizona College of Medicine – Phoenix is much like the city it calls home, emerging. Being relatively new, having opened in 2007, the campus maintains the close-knit feel that makes it such a welcome destination to new and prospective students. Yet that is not the only thing that makes the culture here so special.

The college remains steadfast in its pursuit to provide quality medical education. This is demonstrated through its desire to stay up to date with the latest academic, health care and technological trends, as well as in its partnerships with the health care community and the City of Phoenix itself.

Looking to the future, the college is eager to continue embracing the ever-changing landscape of health care in the 21st century. More importantly, the college will continue to strive to not only produce exceptional physicians, but well-rounded and quality individuals, as well.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: A car is not required but is helpful for getting students to and from clinical sites located throughout the valley.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Professional dress required for all patient interactions and mandatory lectures.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: A free peer-tutoring and supplemental program exists to support student success and faculty office hours are available on an open door basis and through email.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Begins week 2 of school, continues every week throughout years 1 and 2. View: https://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/cce
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Small group, Cadaveric dissections, BioPac medical physiology laboratories, patient panels, clinical case mysteries, team-based learning, independent learning modules, and flipped classroom.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Clerkship rotations begin in April of the second year, giving students extra time to explore specialties before having to design a fourth-year schedule and before applying to residencies.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Generally, attendance at lectures is not required.  However, attendance may be mandatory for specific classes (ex: when patients are present for a panel).
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The UA College of Medicine – Phoenix embraces the opportunities to optimize its curriculum and its delivery to the students. The organ systems-based block curriculum in the preclerkship years (Years 1 & 2) will retain many of its strengths, including being taught in an integrated manner by basic scientists and clinicians working side-by-side. Other proven aspects of the block curriculum will also remain central to its teaching mission:
1.	Small group, case-based Instruction (CBI)
2.	Cadaveric dissection laboratories
3.	BioPac medical physiology laboratories
4.	Patient panels
5.	Clinical case mysteries small group presentations
6.	Team-based learning
7.	Independent learning modules
8.	Flipped classroom methodologies

More information regarding our curriculum can be found at: https://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/md-curriculum
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms:
The college introduced a  3-year MD option, the Primary Care Accelerated Program (PCAP), that offers students an early and seamless transition into a primary care residency in Arizona. The curriculum involves accelerated and intensive learning experiences with a clear focus on primary care. Primary care specialties included in the program:  Family Medicine, General Pediatrics, and General Internal Medicine. Visit https://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/md-program/3-year-md-pcap for more information.
The college also established the Primary Care Scholarship Program to help address the urgent need for physicians in the state by covering tuition associated with medical education for those willing, in exchange, to practice primary care in a a rural or urban underserved community in Arizona. Visit https://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/pcp-scholarship for more information.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: As an integral part of an academic medical center, the University of Arizona College of Medicine – Phoenix focuses on advancing the intersection of research, education and clinical care. This tripartite approach combines leading-edge research, innovative and personalized instruction, and patient-centered care to achieve the best outcomes for patients. Visit https://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/research for more information.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Various opportunities allow medical students to serve through provision of clinical care, health education and mentoring. Visit: https://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/chip
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: The UA College of Medicine - Phoenix works with partner hospitals and other health-care facilities throughout the Phoenix area. View: http://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/partners/clinical
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
Years 1 and 2: Pass/Fail 
Years 3 and 4:Pass/Fail/High Pass and Honors

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
Throughout the College’s journey of creation, we have held and continue to have an expansive vision for the future. We value our past, are proud of our accomplishments to date and believe that collectively, our future is framed by how expansive our vision is and limited only by boundaries we place on these dreams.

The College of Medicine – Phoenix is committed to four pillars that empower its mission and vision for the future. The Education Pillar, Research Pillar, Clinical Pillar and Community Service Pillar converge in many areas and synergistically form the foundation of the College.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: The University of Arizona College of Medicine – Phoenix inspires and trains exemplary physicians, scientists and leaders to optimize health and health care in Arizona and beyond. We are uniquely positioned to accelerate the biomedical and economic engines in Phoenix and the State by leveraging our vital relationships with key clinical and community partners.
medSchoolInformation.videoTitle: University of Arizona College of Medicine – Phoenix Campus Tour
medSchoolInformation.videoDescription: We invite you to take a look at our campus and the surrounding city of Phoenix through the eyes of our faculty and staff.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: The College requires a copy of the AAMC-facilitated Criminal Background check completed at acceptance and the Arizona Department of Public Safety Fingerprint Clearance Card (FCC).
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: Final decision due by April 30, 2027. If a student is admitted after this date, they have 5 business days from the date of the offer to respond.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: The admissions committee requires a minimum of three letters from individuals with whom you have an established professional relationship and can clearly affirm the traits and characteristics desired in a physician. At least one letter from a recent clinical experience is highly recommended. Additional letters from individuals in a variety of settings are desired: employer, research lab supervisor, community service project leader, etc.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: At least one letter from a recent clinical experience is highly recommended. Additional letters from individuals in a variety of settings are desired: employer, research lab supervisor, community service project leader, etc. Letters from family members or personal friends are not recommended.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: More information regarding the interview day can be found at https://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/mmi
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: The Multiple Mini-Interview (MMI), a series of 5-stations lasting 7-minutes each, are administered by the College. MMIs provide additional information to the admissions committee regarding the applicants' qualifications.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Applicants with US Citizenship or Permanent Resident status who have a cumulative and science GPA of 3.6 and MCAT test score of at least 506 recorded between January 2023 and September 12, 2026.
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: No later than 30 days from the date of the invite or December 1, 2026, whichever date is soonest.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Students may be eligible for state residency after enrollment. For more information please visit http://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/admission-requirements/additional/residency
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: Must be a US citizen or permanent resident.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Applicants must have taken the MCAT exam within four years of intended matriculation into medical school. To be considered for admission into the entering class of 2027, applicants must have taken the MCAT between January 2023 and September 12, 2026.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: The college has established a minimum composite score of a 506 for the MCAT. All MCAT scores are visible to the Admissions Committee, regardless of the date taken.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: Applicants must have a cumulative science (BCPM) and overall GPA of 3.6 or better in either their undergraduate, post-baccalaureate, or graduate studies.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: There is no minimum undergraduate GPA required to consider an applicant's postbacc or graduate coursework.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: We recommend 18+ completed credit hours at time of application in order to consider an applicant's postbacc or graduate coursework.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: All coursework from regionally accredited community colleges are accepted toward our admissions requirements. However, we do require at least one of the science prerequisite courses be completed as an upper-division (junior or senior-level) course which typically needs to be fulfilled through a 4-year college/university.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: While letters of interest/intent are not generally accepted, students offered a position on the waitlist at the end of the season may submit these letters to supplement their application.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: All students must possess the capability to complete, with or without reasonable accommodations, the entire curriculum established by the College of Medicine – Phoenix. The curriculum requires demonstrated proficiency in a variety of cognitive, problem-solving, communicative and interpersonal skills. To achieve these proficiencies, the College of Medicine – Phoenix requires that each student be able to meet the following essential qualifications/technical standards: motor skills, sensory/observation, communication, cognitive, behavioral/social, and professional conduct. Information about these and other important skills and disability resources is included on our website.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The Arizona Board of Regents sets tuition during the spring of each academic year; therefore, the 2026-2027 tuition and fees will be set in late spring of 2026. 

You can review a typical medical student's Cost of Attendance by visiting https://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/md-program/cost-attendance
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Some out-of-state students are eligible for in-state tuition based on certain exceptions: Married to an AZ resident, Military Stationed in AZ, Military Honorable Discharge, Native American (federally-recognized with identification).  Visit http://registrar.arizona.edu/personal-information/general-residency-guidelines.

medSchoolPrograms.name: The MD-MPH Dual Degree Program is offered jointly by the College of Medicine – Phoenix and the UArizona Mel and Enid Zuckerman College of Public Health at the Phoenix Biomedical Campus.
medSchoolPrograms.programLength: Students are concurrently enrolled in the MPH and MD programs and can typically complete both degrees in four years.
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: Students apply to the MD-MPH dual degree program during their first year of medical school.

medSchoolPrograms.info: More information regarding all dual degree programs can be found at http://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/md-dual-degrees

The mission of the Pathway Scholars Program is to provide a holistic foundation for Arizona pre-med students to succeed in the rigors of medical school at the College of Medicine – Phoenix. Community-based education for the physician workforce is the driving goal of the program, recognizing that patient needs are best met when providers respect the wealth of values within our community and identify with patients' individuality. Moreover, this program exists to provide academic support, leadership development, and a dedicated community for students who have experienced unique or greater-than-average challenges in preparing to become competitive medical school applicants.

To learn more regarding eligibility, application process and timeline, please visit http://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/pathway

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: The 3-year MD: Primary Care Accelerated Program (PCAP) is a rigorous program designed for students with a clear commitment to primary care. Developed by the University of Arizona College of Medicine – Phoenix in collaboration with local primary care residency partners, PCAP offers a unique, integrated path from undergraduate medical education (medical school) to graduate medical education (residency).
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Applicants to this program must be US citizens or permanent residents.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationDeadline: September 1, 2026 for students planning to start medical school in 2027.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq: The 3-year MD Primary Care Accelerated Program (PCAP) is designed for students interested in practicing Primary Care in Arizona. This 3-year accelerated medical school curriculum is focused on rural, Tribal and Underserved communities in Arizona and will be coupled with existing residency programs throughout Arizona. So, three years for medical school and three years for residency, a “3+3” model.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option for all Three-Year MD students
medSchoolMdPathway.resAdditionalInfo: Students who meet performance benchmarks can transition into a partnering primary care residency program in Arizona upon graduation from medical school, using a modified and simplistic match process.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Required courses for admission may be in-progress during the application process; however courses must be completed and recorded on an official transcript no later than June 15, 2027. Prerequisites must be completed at a regionally accredited institution and earn a minimum of 2 credits with a grade of C (2.0) or higher. Labs are not required for the sciences prerequisites and online courses are acceptable, as long as they meet the above criteria.

Students who have earned a degree outside the U.S. or Canada are required to complete a minimum of 60 credit hours at an accredited educational institution located in the U.S. or Canada, including all required courses for admission.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We do not have a recency requirement for the completion of prerequisite coursework.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors:
The selection of students is aligned with the mission and core value of the University of Arizona College of Medicine - Phoenix.  Central to our mission is the desire to inspire and train individuals who will:

1. Be life-long learners and inquisitive scholars
2. Be exemplary physicians, scientists and leaders
3. Embrace professionalism, innovation and collaboration to optimize health and health care for all

The Admissions Committee follows a holistic review process seeking applicants that demonstrate academic, professional, and personal readiness for medicine. Core competencies in 5 different areas (clinical exposure, leadership, research, community service, and extracurricular activities) are considered during the review process. The committee has also identified 16 personal attributes and characteristics deemed essential for our curriculum. More information can be found at https://phoenixmed.arizona.edu/admission-requirements
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: We strongly recommend students gain experience in medically related volunteer and/or paid positions that provide an understanding of the patient-physician relationship.
